P^n→r pointwise, so invariance and bounded convergence force every P-invariant probability to be supported on the fixed set S; conversely all measures there are invariant. Exchanging I and J produces exactly the claimed simplex and all pointwise empirical limits. Two affine inverse-image lengths are both 1−3δ/2, giving normalized basin 4−6δ; at δ=2/3 P is identity, giving no positive-measure basins. Exact geometric thresholds give the transient distribution. value.rationale: The original source singled out the δ=1/2 attracting core and raised general core-measure existence questions. The exact natural family phase diagram finds an immediate loss of invariant-measure uniqueness, a unique physical branch whose normalized basin shrinks as 4−6δ, complete loss of physical measures at δ=2/3, and a parameter-universal transient law. This resolves actual behavior of a motivated entire parameter interval, not an arbitrary finite computation or a restatement of the δ=1/2 example.
